task: Build src/features/node_features.py — the Phase 2 node-feature module that collapses the daily price panel into a [T, N, F] tensor of cross-sectionally standardised asset descriptors sampled on a monthly rebalance clock.

context.project: Dynamic equity clustering with temporal GNNs.
context.repo_root: the current working directory; run all commands from here
context.input: data/processed/panel.parquet — long format, columns: date, ticker, open, high, low, close, volume, dollar_volume, log_ret, is_filled. Verified dense: 105 tickers x 2929 sessions, 2015-01-02 to 2026-08-26, zero NaNs in close.
context.core_idea: There are two clocks. The DAILY clock carries returns and volumes. The REBALANCE clock (month-end) carries graphs, embeddings and clusters. A node feature is a function collapsing a trailing window of the daily clock into one number, evaluated on the rebalance clock. Compute every feature on the full daily clock first, then sample on rebalance dates. Do not loop over rebalance dates recomputing windows — it is far slower and invites off-by-one alignment bugs.
context.design_boundary: These are NODE features: marginal properties of a single asset. Pairwise quantities (correlation, partial correlation, co-movement) are EDGE features and belong in Phase 3 (src/graphs/). Do not compute any pairwise quantity in this module. beta_252 and idio_vol_252 are the deliberate exception: they are computed against a market aggregate but describe the asset's own character.

leakage_constraints.priority: These are the highest-priority constraints in this task. A leaked feature produces coherent-looking clusters that are worthless, and unlike a supervised task there is no accuracy metric that will reveal it.
rules: Every rolling window must be right-aligned and backward-looking. X[t] may use data on (-inf, t] only.
Never pass center=True to any rolling or expanding call.
Never use a negative shift. shift(-k) is forbidden anywhere in this module.
Never use bfill, backfill, or interpolate with a method that reads forward.
Cross-sectional standardisation operates across tickers at a single date (axis=1). It must never operate across time.
Add a module-level docstring section stating these rules.

functions.name: build_features
functions.spec: Compute all fifteen features on the daily clock. Return {feature_name: DataFrame(date x ticker)}. Call market_beta for the two factor features (it will raise NotImplementedError until the user fills it in — that is expected and acceptable).

functions.name: standardise
functions.spec: Robust cross-sectional standardisation at each date (axis=1). Centre on the row median, scale by row MAD * 1.4826 (the Gaussian consistency constant), then clip to +/- winsor. Clipping MUST be the final operation: nothing may re-centre, re-scale or otherwise transform the values after the clip. Rescaling after clipping silently undoes it -- on a zero-inflated feature the post-clip MAD is near zero, so dividing by it pushes values back past the bound (observed: max 7.28 at winsor 3.0). The clip bound is a hard guarantee, not an approximation. Use median/MAD rather than mean/std because std is inflated by the very outliers being clipped, so a mean/std clip barely bites. Guard against zero MAD (a degenerate cross-section) by falling back to the row std, and if that is also zero return zeros for that row.

functions.name: assemble
functions.signature: assemble(features: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], dates: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[str], list[str]]
functions.spec: Standardise each feature, sample it on the rebalance dates, and stack into X of shape [T, N, F] with axis order (date, ticker, feature). Return (X, tickers, feature_names). Count residual NaNs and print the count per feature BEFORE filling; fill remaining NaNs with 0.0 (which places the asset at the cross-sectional centre) and print the total filled as a fraction of X.size. Assert the final X contains no NaN or inf.

functions.name: feature_correlation
functions.spec: Pool across all dates and tickers (reshape to [T*N, F]) and return the F x F Pearson correlation matrix as a labelled DataFrame.

feature_definitions.note: Fifteen features. All windows in trading days. Annualisation factor TRADING_DAYS = 252. Every rolling call uses min_periods = int(0.8 * window).

risk.vol_21: rolling 21d std of log_ret, times sqrt(252)
risk.vol_63: rolling 63d std of log_ret, times sqrt(252)
risk.semivol_63: rolling 63d std computed over negative log returns only (mask positives to NaN first), times sqrt(252)
risk.volofvol_63: rolling 63d std of the 21d rolling vol series
risk.kurt_252: rolling 252d excess kurtosis of log_ret (pandas .kurt() is already excess)

liquidity.log_adv_63: log of the rolling 63d mean of dollar_volume. The log is mandatory: dollar volume spans orders of magnitude and untransformed it behaves as a single-name outlier detector rather than a feature.
liquidity.amihud_63: build the daily ratio |log_ret| / dollar_volume, take its rolling 63d mean, then take the log. dollar_volume is already NaN where non-positive (handled in clean.py), so no additional zero guard is needed, but assert no inf appears. The log is mandatory: Amihud is severely right-skewed.
liquidity.zero_ret_frac_63: rolling 63d mean of the indicator (abs(log_ret) < 1e-8). A crude but effective illiquidity proxy.

excluded_by_default.note: Computed and standardised as usual, then dropped in assemble via config features.exclude. They remain defined so the decision stays visible and reversible.
excluded_by_default.amihud_63: Correlates -0.962 with log_adv_63. Dollar volume is the denominator of Amihud, so with |log_ret| varying far less than volume the log of one is very nearly the negative log of the other. The pair is definitionally near-duplicate and carries roughly one dimension of signal, not two.
excluded_by_default.zero_ret_frac_63: Zero-inflated: over 75% of values are exactly zero on this universe (measured: 77.6%). A feature that is constant across most of the cross-section contributes no separating information to a distance-based clusterer, and its few non-zero values dominate the standardised scale.

trend.mom_252_21: skip-month momentum: rolling 252d sum of log_ret MINUS rolling 21d sum of log_ret. This excludes the most recent month, which is standard because recent-month returns tend to reverse rather than continue.

tests.constraint: Use small synthetic DataFrames built inline. Do NOT read data/processed/panel.parquet — a test that reads real data is a description of today's dataset, not a test of the code.
cases: realised_vol: a series of i.i.d. normal returns with known sigma recovers approximately sigma * sqrt(252), within a generous tolerance.
mom_252_21: on a series with constant daily return r, the value equals exactly 231 * r, confirming the most recent 21 days are excluded.

standardise: output satisfies abs(z).max() <= winsor exactly; this is a test of the clipping guarantee itself, not a proxy for it. A row containing one extreme outlier has that outlier clipped to the winsor bound.
standardise: a row of identical values returns zeros rather than NaN or inf (degenerate cross-section guard).
dist_52w_high: is always <= 0, and equals 0 exactly on the day a series makes a new rolling maximum.

no_lookahead: a canary test — build a returns frame, compute vol_63, corrupt the LAST row of returns to an extreme value, recompute, and assert that all feature values strictly before that date are unchanged. This is the single most important test in the file.
